title: Achma (Georgian layered cheese pastry)

ingredients.name: sulguni cheese, grated (or low-moisture mozzarella mixed with a little feta)
Imeruli cheese, crumbled (or soaked mild feta)

steps: Whisk the eggs with the water and salt, add the flour and knead into a smooth, fairly stiff dough. Rest it for 30 minutes under a bowl.
Divide the dough into 8 portions and roll each as thin as you can into a rectangle roughly the size of your baking dish.

Boil the sheets one at a time in a large pot of salted water for about a minute each, then lift them into a bowl of cold water and drain on clean towels. Brush each lightly with melted butter so they do not stick together.
Toss the two cheeses together. Heat the oven to 200 C and butter a rectangular baking dish.
Lay one sheet in the dish, scatter a thin layer of cheese and drizzle with butter. Repeat, folding the edges of each sheet as needed, until you have used everything and finish with a cheese layer.
Pour the remaining butter over the top and bake for 30 to 35 minutes until golden and bubbling at the edges.
Rest for 10 minutes so the layers settle, then cut into squares and serve warm.

title: Adjarian khachapuri (boat-shaped cheese bread with egg)

ingredients.name: sulguni cheese, grated (or 250 g mozzarella mixed with 150 g feta)

steps: Stir the flour, yeast, sugar and salt together, then add the yoghurt, lukewarm water and oil and knead for about 8 minutes into a soft, slightly tacky dough.
Cover the dough and leave it somewhere warm for 1 hour, until doubled in size.
Heat the oven to its highest setting, 230 C or more, with a baking tray inside. Mix the grated cheese with the whole egg.

Divide the dough into four and roll each piece into an oval about 25 cm long. Pile the cheese along the middle, leaving a rim, then roll the two long edges inward and pinch the ends together to form a boat with a pointed bow and stern.
Bake the boats for 10 to 12 minutes until the crust is golden and the cheese is bubbling.
Pull them out, make a shallow well in the cheese, and slide a yolk into each boat. Return to the oven for 1 to 2 minutes so the yolk only just warms.
Top each boat with a cube of butter and serve at once. Stir the yolk and butter into the molten cheese and tear off the crust to dip.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Ajapsandali (Georgian aubergine and vegetable stew)
steps: Salt the aubergine cubes, leave them for 20 minutes, then rinse and pat dry to remove bitterness.
Heat half the oil in a wide, deep pan and fry the aubergine in batches until golden on the outside, then set aside.
In the same pan, add the remaining oil and fry the onions over medium heat for about 8 minutes until soft and lightly coloured.
Add the potatoes and peppers, fry for 5 minutes, then stir in the tomatoes, garlic, chilli, ground coriander and blue fenugreek.
Cover and simmer gently for 15 minutes, stirring now and then, until the potatoes are nearly tender.
Return the aubergine to the pan, add salt and half the herbs, and simmer for another 15 minutes, uncovered, until the stew is thick and glossy.
Stir in the remaining fresh herbs and serve warm or cold, with bread.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Ajika (Georgian hot pepper and herb paste)

ingredients.name: hot red chilli peppers, deseeded for a milder paste
dried marigold petals, crumbled (or a pinch of turmeric)

steps: Wear gloves, then trim and roughly chop all the peppers. Remove the seeds from the chillies if you want less heat.
Put the peppers, garlic and fresh coriander through a meat grinder with a fine plate, or blitz them in a food processor in short pulses until you have a coarse paste.
Stir in the ground coriander, blue fenugreek, dill, marigold and salt.
Mix in the vinegar and let the paste stand for 30 minutes so the flavours blend.
Taste and adjust the salt and heat, then pack the paste into clean jars.
Press it down, cover the surface with a thin film of oil and keep it in the fridge for up to 3 weeks; stir into soups, stews, beans and marinades, or serve beside grilled meat.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Badrijani Nigvzit (Georgian aubergine rolls with walnut paste)
steps: Slice the aubergines lengthwise into 5 mm slices, sprinkle both sides with salt and leave them in a colander for 30 minutes, then rinse and pat dry.
Fry the slices in batches in hot oil until golden on both sides and soft, then drain on paper towels.
Blitz the walnuts, garlic, coriander, blue fenugreek, fresh coriander and a pinch of salt in a food processor, then add the vinegar and enough warm water to make a smooth paste.
Spread a spoonful of the walnut paste along each cooled aubergine slice.
Roll each slice up from the narrow end, or fold it over, and arrange the rolls on a platter.
Top with pomegranate seeds, a little extra paste and fresh herbs, and serve at room temperature or chilled.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Bazhe (Georgian walnut sauce)

ingredients.name: warm water or light chicken stock

steps: Grind the walnuts as finely as you can in a food processor or mortar until they start to release their oil.
Add the garlic and salt and keep working it into a thick paste.
Add the coriander, blue fenugreek, marigold and cayenne, and mix thoroughly.
Pour in the vinegar, then thin the paste gradually with warm water or stock, stirring until it falls between sour cream and gravy in thickness.
Taste for salt, sourness and heat, then leave it for at least an hour so the flavours settle.
Serve at room temperature over cold poultry, boiled potatoes or fried fish, or use it as the sauce for satsivi.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Chakapuli (Georgian lamb and tarragon stew)

ingredients.name: lamb shoulder or ribs, on the bone, cut into pieces
sour green plums, halved (or 3 tbsp tkemali sauce plus a squeeze of lemon)

steps: Put the lamb in a heavy pot with the butter and a little salt, and cook gently, covered, for 20 minutes so the meat gives up its own juices. Do not brown it.
Scatter half of the tarragon, spring onions, garlic and chilli over the lamb.
Pour in the wine and enough water to just cover the lamb, bring to a boil, then lower the heat and simmer, covered, for about 1 hour.
Add the sour plums and simmer for another 30 minutes until the lamb is very tender and the plums have softened and thickened the broth.
Stir in the rest of the tarragon, the coriander, spring onions and garlic and cook for 5 more minutes; adjust the salt.
Serve in deep bowls with hot bread or boiled potatoes.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Chakhokhbili (Georgian chicken and tomato stew)

ingredients.name: chicken pieces on the bone (thighs and drumsticks are best)
ripe tomatoes, peeled and chopped (or one 800 g tin)

steps: Salt the chicken pieces. Place them skin side down in a wide dry pan over medium heat and brown them in their own fat for about 10 minutes per side.
Remove the chicken and pour off most of the fat. Add the butter or oil and cook the onions slowly for 10 minutes until soft and golden.
Return the chicken to the pan, add the tomatoes, khmeli suneli, blue fenugreek and chilli.
Cover and simmer for about 35 minutes until the chicken is tender and the sauce has thickened, stirring occasionally.
Add the garlic and half the herbs and cook for 5 minutes more.
Stir in the remaining fresh herbs, check the salt, and serve with bread or boiled potatoes.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Chanakhi (Georgian lamb and aubergine pot)

ingredients.name: lamb shoulder, cut into 4 cm pieces, bone in if possible
potatoes, peeled and cut into chunks

steps: Heat the oven to 160 C. Salt the aubergines for 15 minutes, then rinse and pat dry.
Melt the butter in a clay pot or heavy casserole and add the lamb with a little salt.
Layer the onions, then the aubergines, then the potatoes over the lamb, seasoning each layer lightly.
Top with the tomatoes, garlic, chilli and half the herbs, then pour the water down the side of the pot.
Cover and cook in the oven for about 2 hours 30 minutes, until the lamb is fall-apart tender and the vegetables are soft; do not stir, so the layers stay distinct.
Scatter the remaining herbs on top and serve straight from the pot with bread and fresh cheese.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Chashushuli (Georgian beef and tomato stew)

ingredients.name: beef or veal (shoulder or chuck), cut into 3 cm cubes
ripe tomatoes, peeled and chopped (or 400 g tinned)
mixed fresh coriander (cilantro), parsley and dill, chopped

steps: Heat the oil in a heavy pot and brown the beef in batches over high heat until deeply coloured, then return it all to the pot.
Add the onions and cook for 8 minutes, stirring, until they soften.
Pour in the hot water, cover and simmer on low for 45 minutes.
Add the tomatoes, tomato paste, ajika, khmeli suneli, ground coriander and salt, and simmer, covered, for another 45 minutes until the beef is tender.
Uncover and cook for 10 minutes to thicken the sauce, then stir in the garlic.
Take the pot off the heat, stir in the fresh herbs and serve with potatoes, mchadi or bread.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Chicken Tabaka (Georgian pan-pressed chicken)
steps: Remove the backbone from the chicken and open it flat, pressing hard on the breastbone. Rub salt and pepper into both sides.
Heat the oil and half the butter in a very large heavy frying pan over medium heat.
Lay the chicken skin side down, cover it with a lid or plate and set a heavy weight, such as a second pan or foil-wrapped bricks, on top.
Cook for about 20 minutes until the skin is deep golden and crisp, then flip, replace the weight and cook for another 15 to 20 minutes until the juices run clear.
Move the chicken to a board. In the same pan, soften the garlic in the remaining butter for 1 minute, then pour in the hot stock and lemon juice and simmer for 3 minutes.
Stir in the coriander, cut the chicken into portions and spoon the garlic sauce over, or serve with tkemali.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Chikhirtma (Georgian chicken and egg soup)

ingredients.name: chicken thighs and drumsticks, bone in
dried marigold petals or a pinch of saffron

steps: Put the chicken in a pot with the water, bring to a boil, skim off the foam, then simmer for about 45 minutes until the meat is tender. Lift the chicken out and shred it, discarding skin and bones.
Melt the butter in a pan and cook the onions gently until soft but not browned. Stir in the flour and cook for 1 minute.
Ladle in a few spoonfuls of the hot broth, whisking to a smooth paste, then return everything to the pot with the rest of the broth.
Add the marigold or saffron and simmer for 10 minutes.

Beat the egg yolks with the vinegar in a bowl. Whisking constantly, add a ladle of hot broth, then pour the mixture back into the pot in a thin stream with the heat very low; do not let it boil or it will curdle.
Return the shredded chicken to the soup, season with salt and pepper, stir in the herbs and serve at once.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Churchkhela (Georgian grape juice and walnut candle)

ingredients.name: thick cotton thread and a long sturdy needle

steps: Cut the thread into 40 cm lengths and knot one end of each around a small piece of wood or a button. Thread 8 to 10 walnut halves onto each, leaving a loop at the top for hanging.
Pour the grape juice into a wide pot, bring it to a boil and simmer until reduced by about one quarter.
Whisk the flour with a little cold grape juice, or water, until smooth, then pour it into the pot in a thin stream, stirring constantly. Add the sugar if using.
Cook over low heat, stirring without a break, for about 20 minutes until the mixture is thick like a glossy pudding. This is called tatara.
Let it cool a few minutes, then dip each string of walnuts completely into the tatara, lift it and let the excess drip away for a minute.
Hang the strings in a dry, airy spot for a day, then dip them again for a thicker coat. Repeat until you are happy with the layer.
Leave them hanging for 1 to 2 weeks until firm but still chewy, then wrap and keep in a cool place.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Elarji (Mingrelian cornmeal and cheese porridge)

ingredients.name: sulguni cheese, sliced thin (or low-moisture mozzarella with a little feta)

steps: Bring the water and salt to a boil in a heavy pot.
Pour in the cornmeal in a thin stream while stirring with a wooden spoon, to avoid lumps.
Lower the heat and cook for about 15 minutes, stirring often, until the porridge pulls away from the sides of the pot. This is the base called ghomi.
Add the cheese slices a handful at a time, beating hard with the spoon so the cheese melts into the porridge.
Keep stirring and stretching the mass for 5 to 8 minutes until it becomes smooth, elastic and stringy; if it stiffens too much, loosen with a splash of hot water.
Pile it onto a warm plate, make a hollow in the centre, add the butter, and serve immediately while it is still stretchy.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Gebzhalia (Mingrelian cheese rolls with mint)

ingredients.name: sulguni cheese (or low-moisture mozzarella), thinly sliced
nadugi or ricotta (or fresh curd cheese)

steps: Heat the water to about 80 C. Drop in the cheese slices a few at a time, and stir with a wooden spoon until they melt together into a smooth stretchy mass.
Lift the melted cheese out, knead it briefly until smooth and roll it out between two sheets of baking paper into a thin rectangle.
Mash half of the mint with the garlic, the nadugi and the salt to make a soft filling.
Spread the filling thinly across the cheese sheet and roll it up tightly like a swiss roll.
Chill the roll for 1 hour, then slice it into rounds about 2 cm thick.
Beat the yoghurt with the remaining mint and a pinch of salt, thin it with a spoonful of milk if needed, and serve it alongside the rolls.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Gozinaki (Georgian walnut and honey brittle)

ingredients.name: vegetable oil, for greasing the board and knife

steps: Toast the walnuts in a dry pan over medium heat for 5 to 6 minutes until fragrant, shaking often, then set aside.
Heat the honey and sugar together in a wide pan over low heat, stirring, and let it bubble gently for 8 to 10 minutes until it darkens slightly and thickens.
Add the warm walnuts and stir for 2 to 3 minutes until every piece is evenly coated and the mixture holds together.
Tip it onto an oiled board or marble slab and, working quickly with a wet or oiled spatula, press it out to a 1.5 cm thick layer.
While it is still warm, cut it with an oiled knife into diamonds.
Leave it to cool completely and set, then lift the pieces away and store in an airtight tin.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Guruli Gvezeli (Gurian cheese and egg pie)

ingredients.name: Imeruli cheese, grated (or feta mixed with mozzarella)

steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, then add the milk and water and knead for about 8 minutes into a soft dough. Cover and leave it to rise for 1 hour.
Fry the quartered eggs briefly in a little butter, or dry them in a warm oven for 15 minutes, until lightly coloured; this stands in for the old smoking over the hearth.
Heat the oven to 200 C and line a baking tray.
Divide the dough into 4 balls and roll each into a circle about 20 cm across.
Spread cheese over one half of each circle and set 4 egg quarters on top, leaving the edge clear.
Fold the dough over into a crescent and press and crimp the edges to seal tightly.
Brush with melted butter and bake for 20 to 25 minutes until golden, then brush again with butter and serve warm.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Imeretian khachapuri (round cheese-filled bread)

ingredients.name: sulguni cheese, grated (or 250 g mozzarella mixed with 150 g feta)

steps: Stir the flour, yeast, sugar and salt together, then add the yoghurt, lukewarm water and oil and knead for about 8 minutes into a soft, slightly tacky dough.
Cover the dough and leave it somewhere warm for 1 hour, until doubled in size.
Heat the oven to 220 C. Mix the grated cheese with the egg until it holds together; if the cheese is very salty, rinse or soak it first.
Divide the dough into two pieces. Roll one into a circle about 24 cm across, and heap half the filling in the centre.

Gather the edges up over the filling like a purse and pinch to seal, then turn it seam-side down and press and roll it out gently into a flat round about 1.5 cm thick, without letting the cheese break through.
Place on a lined tray, prick the top once or twice, and brush with melted butter. Make the second one the same way.
Bake for 15 to 18 minutes until golden, brush again with butter, and serve warm in wedges.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Kharcho (Georgian beef, rice and walnut soup)

ingredients.name: beef on the bone (brisket or shin), cut into big pieces
tkemali sour plum puree (or 3 tbsp tkemali sauce, or 80 g tklapi dissolved in hot water)

steps: Put the beef and water in a pot, bring to a boil, skim the foam, then simmer, covered, for about 1 hour 30 minutes until the meat is tender. Remove the beef, cut it into bite-size pieces, discard any bones, and keep the broth.
Cook the onions in the butter or oil over medium heat for 8 minutes until golden.
Return the onions and beef to the broth and bring it back to a simmer.
Stir in the rice and cook for about 10 minutes.
Add the walnuts, tkemali puree, khmeli suneli, ground coriander, blue fenugreek and marigold, and simmer for another 15 minutes until the rice is soft and the soup is thick.
Add the garlic and fresh coriander, taste for salt and sourness, and cook for 2 more minutes.
Let the soup rest off the heat for 10 minutes before serving with bread.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Khashlama (Georgian boiled beef)

ingredients.name: beef (brisket, short rib or chuck), in large pieces, bone in if possible
tkemali sauce and boiled potatoes, to serve

steps: Put the beef in a deep pot, cover with hot water, bring to a boil for 5 minutes and then pour off the water and rinse the meat.
Return the beef to the pot, add fresh cold water to cover and the halved onion, and bring to a boil. Skim off the foam.
Partly cover and simmer very gently for about 1 hour without adding salt.
Add the garlic, bay leaves and peppercorns and keep simmering for 1 1/2 to 2 hours more, until the meat is tender enough to fall off the bone.
Add the coarse salt in the last 15 minutes of cooking.
Lift the meat onto a platter, scatter with parsley and serve hot with boiled potatoes and tkemali, saving the broth for soup.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Khinkali (Georgian soup dumplings)

ingredients.name: plain flour, plus extra for rolling
freshly ground black pepper, to serve

steps: Mix the flour and dough salt, pour in the lukewarm water and knead for about 8 minutes into a firm, smooth dough. Cover and rest it for at least 30 minutes.

Combine both minced meats with the grated onion, coriander, caraway, chilli flakes and filling salt, then work in the cold water or stock a little at a time until the mixture feels loose and almost wet. This liquid turns into the broth inside each dumpling.
Divide the dough into about 24 pieces. Roll each into a circle roughly 12 cm across, keeping the centre a bit thicker and the edges thin.
Put a heaped tablespoon of filling in the middle of a circle. Lift the edge and make small overlapping pleats all the way around, gathering them upward over the filling.
Pinch the pleats together at the top and twist to seal, leaving a small knob of dough, the handle, on top.
Bring a wide pot of salted water to a gentle boil. Lower in the dumplings in batches, nudge them so they do not stick, and simmer for 10 to 12 minutes until they float and the dough is tender.
Lift them out with a slotted spoon and sprinkle generously with black pepper. Eat by holding the knob, biting a small hole to sip the broth first, and discarding the knob.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Khmeli Suneli (Georgian spice blend)

ingredients.name: ground blue fenugreek (utskho suneli) or fenugreek leaves

steps: If your coriander seeds are whole, toast them in a dry pan for 1 to 2 minutes until fragrant, cool, and grind them to a powder.
Crumble the dried herbs, summer savory, dill, basil, mint, parsley and bay leaf, between your fingers, then grind them briefly so they are fine but not dust.
Grind the marigold petals and fenugreek separately.
Combine everything in a bowl and mix thoroughly.
Store in a tightly closed jar away from light; it keeps its aroma for about 3 months, so make small batches.
Use it in stews, bean dishes, chicken and meat marinades, and soups such as kharcho.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Kubdari (Svan meat-filled bread)

ingredients.name: beef, chopped by hand into small pieces
pork shoulder, chopped by hand into small pieces

steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, then work in the egg and warm water and knead for 8 minutes into a soft dough. Cover and let it rise for 1 hour.

Combine the beef, pork, onion, garlic, cumin, coriander, blue fenugreek, pepper flakes and Svan salt, and add 3 to 4 tablespoons of cold water. Knead the meat by hand for a few minutes until sticky and juicy.
Heat the oven to 230 C with a baking sheet or stone inside, or heat a heavy frying pan.
Divide the dough into 4 balls and flatten each into a circle about 15 cm wide.
Put a quarter of the filling in the middle of each circle, gather the edges over it and pinch to seal, then flip the parcel and gently roll it out with a rolling pin to about 1 cm thick.
Make a small hole in the top for steam. Bake for 15 to 20 minutes until golden and cooked through, or cook in a covered pan over medium heat for about 10 minutes per side.
Brush with melted butter and serve hot, cut into wedges.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Kuchmachi (Georgian chicken giblets with walnuts and pomegranate)

ingredients.name: salt and chilli flakes to taste

steps: Put the hearts and gizzards in a pot, cover with water, bring to a boil and simmer for about 40 minutes until tender, then drain, reserving 100 ml of the cooking liquid.
Melt half the butter in a pan and cook the onion for 8 minutes until golden.
Add the chopped hearts and gizzards and fry for 5 minutes, then add the livers and cook briefly, about 4 minutes, until just done.
Mix the ground walnuts with the garlic, coriander, blue fenugreek, salt and chilli, and loosen with the reserved liquid and the vinegar.
Stir this walnut mixture into the pan and simmer for 3 to 4 minutes until it forms a thick sauce around the giblets.
Take off the heat, scatter with pomegranate seeds and fresh coriander and serve warm, with bread.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Kupati (Georgian pork sausage)

ingredients.name: pork liver or heart, finely chopped
natural pork sausage casing, soaked (or shape into patties without casing)

steps: Mix the pork, liver or heart, onion, garlic, coriander, blue fenugreek, paprika, ajika and salt thoroughly with your hands until the mixture becomes tacky.
Fold in the pomegranate seeds gently, so they stay whole.
Fry a small spoonful to taste, and adjust salt and heat if needed.
Rinse the soaked casing, tie off one end and fill it with the mixture using a sausage horn or funnel, twisting off links about 12 cm long. Prick any air pockets.
Rest the sausages in the fridge for a few hours or overnight to firm up.
Fry them in a heavy pan over low heat with a splash of water, covered, for about 12 minutes, then uncover and brown for 5 minutes until cooked through.
Serve with tkemali or satsebeli, raw onion and bread.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Lobiani (Georgian bean-stuffed bread)

ingredients.name: dried red kidney beans, soaked overnight (or 2 cans, 400 g each, drained)
butter or oil, for the onions
salt and pepper, and extra butter for brushing

steps: Mix the flour, yeast, sugar and salt, add the milk, water and oil, and knead for 8 minutes into a soft dough. Cover and leave it for 1 hour until doubled.
Boil the soaked beans in fresh water for about 1 hour until very tender, then drain; skip this if using canned beans.
Cook the onions in the butter for 10 minutes until soft and golden, add the coriander, then stir in the beans.
Mash the beans coarsely, season well with salt and pepper and let the filling cool to room temperature.
Heat the oven to 220 C. Divide the dough in 4 pieces and flatten each into a round.
Put a quarter of the filling in the centre of each, gather the edges over it, pinch to seal, flip the dough over and roll it out gently to about 1 cm thick, keeping the filling inside.
Prick a few holes in the top, bake for 15 to 20 minutes until golden and brush with butter while hot.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Lobio (Georgian kidney bean stew with walnuts)

ingredients.name: dried red kidney beans, soaked overnight
chilli flakes and salt to taste

steps: Drain the soaked beans, cover with fresh water, add the bay leaf and simmer for 1 to 1 1/2 hours until they are completely soft; do not salt until the end.
Fry the onions in the oil over medium heat for 10 minutes until deeply golden.
Drain the beans but keep the cooking liquid. Mash about two thirds of them roughly, leaving the rest whole.
Add the mashed and whole beans to the onions along with the ground coriander, khmeli suneli, blue fenugreek and a ladle of cooking liquid, and stir.
Mix the walnuts with the garlic and vinegar, stir this into the beans and simmer for 5 to 10 minutes, adding more bean liquid until you have a thick, creamy stew.
Add salt, chilli and most of the coriander, rest for 10 minutes, and serve warm or cold with mchadi or bread, scattered with the remaining fresh coriander.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Mchadi (Georgian cornbread cakes)

ingredients.name: white or yellow cornmeal (fine, stone-ground if possible)

steps: Mix the cornmeal and salt in a large bowl.
Add the warm water a little at a time, mixing with a fork, until the mixture sticks together like damp sand when you squeeze a handful; it should be firm, not sticky.
Let the dough rest for 10 minutes, then check and sprinkle a little more water if it cracks.
With wet hands, form about 8 small round cakes, each about 1.5 cm thick and 8 cm wide.
Heat the oil in a heavy frying pan or cast-iron skillet over medium heat.
Fry the cakes for 4 to 5 minutes on each side, covered if they brown too fast, until golden-brown and crisp outside.
Serve warm with lobio, fresh cheese or pickled vegetables.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Megrelian khachapuri (cheese bread with cheese on top)

ingredients.name: sulguni cheese, grated (or mozzarella and feta)

steps: Stir the flour, yeast, sugar and salt together, then add the yoghurt, lukewarm water and oil and knead for about 8 minutes into a soft, slightly tacky dough.
Cover the dough and leave it somewhere warm for 1 hour, until doubled in size.
Heat the oven to 220 C. Mix 300 g of the cheese with the egg for the filling and keep the other 200 g for the top.
Make a round filled bread exactly as for Imeretian khachapuri: roll a circle, fill the middle, gather the edges, seal, turn over and roll it out to about 1.5 cm thick.
Bake for 12 minutes until the bread is set and starting to colour.
Scatter the reserved cheese over the top and bake for another 5 to 8 minutes until it is melted and speckled with gold.
Cut into wedges and serve hot, while the cheese on top is still stretchy.

source.name: Wikipedia
source.note: Original write-up of a traditional preparation, made for World Recipes. Quantities are approximate; adjust to taste.

title: Mtsvadi (Georgian pork skewers)

ingredients.name: pork neck or shoulder, with some fat, cut into 4 cm cubes
raw onion rings, fresh herbs and tkemali, to serve

steps: Toss the pork with the onion rings, salt, pepper, pomegranate juice and vinegar in a large bowl, squeezing the onion lightly so it releases its juice.
Cover and marinate in the fridge for 3 to 4 hours, or overnight.
Light charcoal, ideally with vine cuttings added, and let it burn down to glowing embers with a bed of grey ash.
Thread the pork onto flat metal skewers, pressing the pieces close together, and discard the onion.
Grill the skewers over hot embers for 10 to 15 minutes, turning every couple of minutes and sprinkling with a little pomegranate juice to calm the flames, until browned outside and juicy within.
Slide the meat off the skewers onto a warm plate and serve with raw onion, fresh herbs, tkemali and bread.

title: Muzhuzhi (Georgian pork aspic)

ingredients.name: white wine vinegar, steeped with a handful of tarragon and basil

steps: Soak the trotters in cold water for 2 hours, then blanch them for 5 minutes in boiling water and rinse.
Cover them with fresh water in a pot, add the onion, bay, peppercorns and salt, and simmer very gently for about 3 hours, skimming off the foam, until the meat is falling off the bone.
In a separate pot cook the pork shoulder in plain water for about 1 hour 15 minutes until tender, then cool it and cut into pieces.
Take the trotter meat from the bones, cut it up and combine it with the shoulder meat in a deep dish, then scatter the garlic over it.
Strain the trotter broth, stir in the tarragon and basil vinegar, and pour it over the meat to cover.
Chill overnight until the aspic sets, then cut it into squares and serve cold with spring onions, fresh herbs and bread.

title: Nadugi (Georgian fresh curd cheese with mint)

ingredients.name: plain full-fat yoghurt or matsoni (not Greek-style)
pomegranate seeds and bread, to serve

steps: Pour the yoghurt into a heavy pot and warm it very slowly to about 70 C, stirring gently now and then, never letting it boil.
Hold it at that temperature for about 20 minutes until the curds separate from the clear whey.
Line a colander with muslin or a clean cloth and ladle the curds into it.
Drain for 1 to 2 hours until you have a soft, moist, ricotta-like curd.
Tip the curds into a bowl, add the salt and beat them lightly until smooth and airy.
Fold in the mint and chilli, chill for an hour and serve as a spread with bread, or with pomegranate seeds.

title: Ojakhuri (Georgian family-style fried pork and potatoes)

ingredients.name: pork shoulder, cut into 3 cm cubes
potatoes, peeled and cut into large chunks
dried marigold petals or khmeli suneli

steps: Heat half of the oil in a large heavy frying pan or cast-iron skillet and fry the pork cubes over high heat until well browned, about 10 minutes.
Add the onions, lower the heat to medium and cook, covered, for 25 minutes, stirring occasionally, until the pork is tender and the onions have melted.
Meanwhile, fry the potato chunks in the remaining oil in a second pan until golden and nearly cooked through, about 15 minutes, stirring often.
Combine the potatoes with the pork, add the garlic, coriander, pepper, marigold or khmeli suneli, and salt.
Cover and cook together for 8 to 10 minutes so the flavours join.
Scatter generously with fresh herbs and serve straight from the pan with pickles or a tomato salad.

title: Pelamushi (Georgian grape juice pudding)

ingredients.name: sugar (optional, if the juice is tart)

steps: Scoop out about 150 ml of the grape juice and whisk it thoroughly with the flour in a bowl until completely smooth.
Pour the remaining juice into a heavy pot and bring it to a gentle boil, adding the sugar if you like.
Lower the heat and slowly pour in the flour mixture, whisking constantly to avoid lumps.
Cook for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring all the time, until the pudding is thick and glossy and leaves a trail when you drag the spoon.
Pour it into a wet dish or individual bowls and let it cool.
Chill for a few hours until it sets, then serve topped with chopped walnuts, or with gozinaki.

title: Pkhali (Georgian spinach and walnut pate)
steps: Blanch the spinach in boiling salted water for 1 to 2 minutes, drain, cool under cold water and squeeze out as much liquid as you can, then chop finely.
Grind the walnuts with the garlic and a pinch of salt in a food processor or mortar until they form a thick paste.
Add the coriander, blue fenugreek, cayenne and vinegar to the walnut paste and blend with a few spoons of water if it is too stiff.
Mix the chopped spinach, onion and fresh coriander with the walnut paste, taste, and adjust salt and vinegar.
Chill the mixture for at least 2 hours so the flavours meld.
Shape into small balls or flat patties, garnish with pomegranate seeds and serve cold with bread. Beetroot, cabbage and green beans can be prepared the same way.

title: Satsebeli (Georgian spicy tomato sauce)

ingredients.name: ripe tomatoes, chopped (or 700 g tinned plum tomatoes)
ajika or hot red pepper flakes

steps: Put the tomatoes in a wide saucepan with a pinch of salt and cook over medium heat for about 20 minutes, crushing them as they soften.
Press the pulp through a coarse sieve to remove skins and seeds, or blend until smooth.
Return the sauce to the pan and simmer for 15 to 20 minutes until reduced to a thin, pourable consistency.
Stir in the coriander, khmeli suneli, blue fenugreek and ajika, and simmer for 3 more minutes.
Take off the heat, add the garlic, vinegar and fresh coriander, and season with salt.
Serve warm or cold with grilled meat, potatoes, eggs, dumplings and bread; it keeps 1 week in the fridge.

title: Satsivi (Georgian chicken in walnut sauce)

ingredients.name: chicken pieces on the bone (or half a small turkey)

steps: Simmer the chicken with the halved onion, salt and water for about 45 minutes until cooked through. Lift out the chicken and strain the broth.
Brown the chicken pieces in a hot pan for a few minutes per side to colour the skin, then set aside.
Soften the chopped onions in the oil or butter for 8 minutes without browning.
Grind the walnuts with the garlic and a pinch of salt in a food processor until very fine and oily, and mix in the coriander, blue fenugreek, marigold, cinnamon, cloves and cayenne.
Stir the walnut mixture into the onions, thin it with about 500 ml of warm broth, and cook very gently for 10 minutes, stirring.
Beat the egg yolks with the vinegar, whisk in a ladle of the hot sauce, then stir it back into the pot over the lowest heat for 2 minutes; do not allow it to boil.
Place the chicken in a deep dish, pour the sauce over it, cool and chill for several hours or overnight; serve cold or at room temperature.

title: Shkmeruli (Georgian chicken in garlic milk sauce)

ingredients.name: chicken pieces on the bone (or a small spatchcocked chicken)
whole milk (or 200 ml milk and 100 ml cream)

steps: Pat the chicken dry and season it all over with salt and pepper.
Heat the oil in a large heavy frying pan over medium heat and brown the chicken, skin side down first, for about 8 to 10 minutes per side until deep golden. Pour off excess fat.
Add the butter and the garlic to the pan and cook for 30 seconds until fragrant but not coloured.
Pour in the milk, scraping up the browned bits, and bring it to a gentle simmer.
Cover and simmer over low heat for 20 to 25 minutes, turning the chicken once, until it is cooked through and the sauce has reduced by about half; do not let it boil hard.
Sprinkle with the fresh herbs and serve with crusty bread or mchadi to mop up the sauce.

title: Shotis Puri (Georgian canoe-shaped bread)
steps: Stir the flour, yeast, salt and sugar together and mix in the warm water to make a soft, slightly sticky dough.
Knead for about 10 minutes until smooth and elastic, then cover and let it rise for 1 hour until doubled.
Place a baking stone or heavy tray in the oven and heat it to the maximum, ideally 250 C, with a tray of hot water on the bottom shelf for steam.
Divide the dough into 2 pieces. Shape each into a long oval, then pinch both ends and curve slightly into a canoe shape, with ends pointed and the middle puffy.
Rest the loaves for 15 minutes, then slash lightly along the length and slide them onto the hot stone.
Bake for 12 to 15 minutes until crisp and deeply golden, and cool on a rack.

title: Spinach Matsoni (Georgian spinach and yoghurt salad)
steps: Steam or boil the spinach for 2 minutes until wilted, then drain and cool.
Squeeze out as much water as possible and chop the spinach very finely.
Mix the crushed garlic with a pinch of salt and stir it into the yoghurt.
Fold the chopped spinach and coriander into the garlic yoghurt.
Season with salt, chill for 30 minutes and serve cold with bread, garnished with pomegranate seeds if you like.

title: Sulguni (Georgian stretched-curd cheese)

ingredients.name: whole cows' milk, pasteurised but not UHT
citric acid, dissolved in 100 ml cool water
liquid rennet, diluted in 50 ml cool water
water, for the hot stretching bath

steps: Warm the milk to 32 C in a large pot, stir in the citric acid solution, and then the diluted rennet, mixing gently with an up-and-down motion for 30 seconds.
Cover and leave undisturbed for 30 to 45 minutes until the curd sets and breaks cleanly over a knife.
Cut the curd into 2 cm cubes and let it rest for 5 minutes, then lift the curds into a colander over a bowl and let the whey drain; keep the whey.
Heat some of the drained whey, or salted water, to about 80 C. Put the curds in a heatproof bowl and pour the hot liquid over them.
Using a wooden spoon, fold and stretch the curd in the hot liquid until it becomes smooth and shiny, about 5 minutes.
Shape the cheese into a flat round disc about 4 cm thick and drop it in cold water for 10 minutes to firm up.

Dissolve the salt in 1 litre of cold water and soak the cheese in this brine for 3 to 6 hours in the fridge, then keep it chilled and eat within a week; it is good fresh, melted in khachapuri and elarji.

title: Svan Salt (Georgian herb and garlic salt)
steps: Toast the coriander and cumin seeds in a dry pan for 1 to 2 minutes until fragrant, then cool completely.
Grind the toasted seeds with the fenugreek, dill, marigold and pepper flakes to a fine powder.
Crush the garlic to a smooth paste with a pinch of the salt.
Mix the garlic paste with the spice powder and the rest of the salt until evenly combined, so the blend is slightly damp.
Pack it into a clean jar. Keep it in the fridge for up to 6 months, and use it on potatoes, fried or grilled meat, eggs, tomatoes and in kubdari.

title: Tarkhuna (Georgian tarragon soda)
steps: Bring the water, sugar, fennel seeds and lemon peel to a simmer in a small pan, stirring until the sugar dissolves.
Add most of the tarragon, pressing it under the surface, and simmer for 2 minutes only so it stays bright.
Pour the mixture into a blender and blitz until the tarragon is finely broken up, then chill for at least 2 hours so the flavour deepens.
Strain through a fine sieve, pressing on the solids, and stir in the lemon juice to make a syrup.
For each glass, pour about 3 tablespoons of syrup over ice and top up with cold sparkling water.
Garnish with a sprig of tarragon. The syrup keeps for a week in the fridge.

title: Tashmijabi (Svan mashed potatoes with cheese)

ingredients.name: sulguni cheese, thinly sliced (or low-moisture mozzarella)

steps: Boil the potatoes in their skins in lightly salted water until tender, about 25 to 30 minutes, then drain, peel and mash them thoroughly.
Return the mash to a heavy pot over low heat, and stir in the milk to loosen it.
Add the cheese slices a few at a time, beating hard with a wooden spoon so the cheese melts into the potatoes.
Keep stirring and stretching the mass for 5 to 7 minutes until it becomes smooth, glossy and elastic.
Season with salt, turn it onto a warm dish and make a hollow in the centre.
Melt the butter and pour it into the hollow; serve straight away, while it is still stretchy.

title: Tkemali (Georgian sour plum sauce)

ingredients.name: sour plums (cherry plums or unripe damsons), stones in
hot red chilli, chopped (or 1 tsp chilli flakes)
sugar, if the plums are very sour (optional)

steps: Put the plums and water in a wide pot, cover and cook on low heat for 15 to 20 minutes until the plums burst and fall apart.
Press the hot plums through a sieve or food mill to remove stones and skins, and return the puree to the pot.
Simmer the puree for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring, until it thickens slightly.
Crush the garlic with the salt, then stir it into the puree with the ground coriander, dried pennyroyal and chilli.
Add the chopped fresh dill and coriander, and simmer for 5 more minutes. Taste and adjust the salt, sourness and heat, adding sugar if needed.
Cool and pour into sterilised jars. Keep it in the fridge for 2 weeks, or heat-process the jars to keep it for the year.

title: Tklapi (Georgian sour plum fruit leather)

ingredients.name: sour cherry plums or tart plums, stoned

steps: Cook the plums with the water in a wide pot over medium-low heat for 20 minutes until completely soft.
Press the fruit through a sieve to remove skins and any stones, and stir in the sugar if you want a sweeter leather.
Simmer the puree for 10 to 15 minutes, stirring often, until thick enough to hold a trail.
Line baking trays with baking paper and spread the puree in a thin, even layer, about 3 mm thick.
Dry in the oven at 60 C with the door slightly ajar for 6 to 10 hours, or in the sun for 2 to 3 days, until the surface is no longer sticky.
Peel the leather off the paper, roll or fold it and store in an airtight container, or hang to dry further.
Use it to sour soups such as kharcho by soaking it in hot water, or eat it as a sour sweet snack.

title: Tonis Puri (Georgian tone-oven bread)
steps: Mix the flour, yeast, salt and sugar in a bowl, add the warm water and stir to a soft dough.
Knead for 10 minutes until smooth, then cover and let it rise for about 1 hour until doubled.
Put a baking stone or inverted heavy baking tray in the oven and heat to the highest setting, around 250 C, with a tray of water at the bottom for steam.
Divide the dough into 2 balls and let them rest for 10 minutes. Stretch each into a slightly oval disc about 2 cm thick, thicker at the edges.
Prick the surface lightly with a fork or your fingertips, which imitates the way the bread is slapped on the walls of the tone.
Slide the loaves onto the hot stone and bake for 10 to 12 minutes until golden, with a crisp bottom and a soft, airy crumb.
Wrap in a cloth for a few minutes and serve warm with cheese, lobio or meat dishes.
